theory.intro: A **net** of a prism is a flat pattern that folds up to make the solid. A right prism has two identical **end faces** (its cross-section) joined by **rectangles**, one rectangle for every side of the end face. So the net of a prism is always **two copies of the base polygon plus a row of rectangles**.
facts: A right prism is named after its cross-section: a **triangular** prism has triangular ends, a **hexagonal** prism has hexagonal ends. A cube and a rectangular prism have rectangular ends.
The net of a prism whose base has $n$ sides is made of **$2$ base polygons** and **$n$ rectangles** (one rectangle per edge of the base).
For a prism with an $n$-sided base: **faces** $= n+2$, **edges** $= 3n$, **vertices** $= 2n$. (A triangular prism has $5$ faces, $9$ edges and $6$ vertices.)
A diagram is a net of a right prism only if it has **exactly two identical end polygons** and the **correct number of rectangles** between them — a missing or spare face means it will not fold up.
When the net folds, each rectangle joins to one edge of the base polygon, so that side of the rectangle equals that side of the base.
steps: Find the two identical polygons in the net — these become the ends; count their sides $n$.
Name the solid as the $n$-sided prism.
If needed, use $n$ to count faces $(n+2)$, edges $(3n)$ and vertices $(2n)$.

foundation.solution_text:
The net has two identical triangles and three rectangles.
Two identical polygons joined by rectangles fold up into a prism, named after that polygon.
The solid is a triangular prism.

The net is made of six rectangles arranged in a cross.
A solid with two identical rectangular ends joined by rectangles is a rectangular prism.
The solid is a rectangular prism.

The net is made of six identical squares in a cross.
Six equal squares fold up into a cube.
The solid is a cube.

The net has two identical six-sided end faces and six rectangles, one for each side of the hexagon.
Two identical hexagons joined by rectangles fold up into a hexagonal prism.
The solid is a hexagonal prism.

foundation.question_text: How many rectangles are in the net of a pentagonal prism, and why?
foundation.solution_text:
A pentagon has $5$ sides, so $n=5$.
The net has one rectangle for each side of the base.
Rectangles $= n$
$= 5$
So the net of a pentagonal prism has $5$ rectangles (plus the two pentagons).

foundation.question_text: A triangular prism has a triangular base, so $n=3$. Find the number of faces, edges and vertices of the prism.
foundation.solution_text:
The base is a triangle, so $n=3$.
Faces $= n+2$
$= 5$
Edges $= 3n$
$= 9$
Vertices $= 2n$
$= 6$

A triangular prism has two triangular ends and three rectangular side faces, one for each side of the triangle.
This diagram has two triangles but only two rectangles.
One rectangular face is missing, so the diagram will not fold up into a triangular prism.

foundation.question_text: A box is a rectangular prism $10$ cm long, $6$ cm wide and $4$ cm high. Its net is made of six rectangles. What are the dimensions of the two largest rectangular faces?
foundation.solution_text:
Each face of the net is a rectangle whose sides are two of the box's dimensions.
The largest faces use the two largest dimensions, $10$ cm and $6$ cm.
The two largest faces (the top and the bottom) are each $10$ cm by $6$ cm.

development.solution_text:
The two identical end faces each have four sides with one pair parallel — they are trapeziums.
There are four rectangles, one for each side of the trapezium.
Two identical trapeziums joined by rectangles fold up into a trapezoidal prism.
The solid is a trapezoidal prism.

development.question_text: A hexagonal prism has a hexagonal base, so $n=6$. Find the number of faces, edges and vertices of the prism.
development.solution_text:
The base is a hexagon, so $n=6$.
Faces $= n+2$
$= 8$
Edges $= 3n$
$= 18$
Vertices $= 2n$
$= 12$

A triangular prism has two triangular ends and three rectangular side faces, so its net needs exactly two triangles and three rectangles.
Net $B$ has three triangles, net $C$ has only two rectangles, and net $D$ has four rectangles.
Only net $A$ has two triangles and three rectangles, so the answer is $A$.

The two identical end faces are triangles, so this should be a triangular prism, which needs exactly three rectangles (one for each side of the triangle).
This diagram has four rectangles.
The extra rectangle would overlap when folded, so the diagram is not a valid net of a right prism.

development.question_text: A triangular prism has a right-angled triangular base with sides $6$ cm, $8$ cm and $10$ cm, and the prism is $12$ cm long. Its net has three rectangles. State the dimensions of each rectangle.
development.solution_text:
Each rectangle joins to one side of the triangle, so its width equals that side and its length equals the prism's length, $12$ cm.
The three sides of the triangle are $6$ cm, $8$ cm and $10$ cm.
The three rectangles are $6\text{ cm}\times 12\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}\times 12\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}\times 12\text{ cm}$.

A rectangular prism has six faces in total, and the strip shows four of them.
Faces needed $= 6-4$
$= 2$
The two missing faces are the side faces, which are rectangles.
Two more rectangles are needed.

development.question_text: A prism has a pentagon as its cross-section. Describe its net: how many of each shape does it contain, and how many faces does the prism have in total?
development.solution_text:
A pentagon has $5$ sides, so $n=5$.
The net has two pentagons (the ends) and one rectangle for each side of the pentagon.
Rectangles $= n$
$= 5$
So the net has $2$ pentagons and $5$ rectangles.
Faces $= n+2$
$= 7$

mastery.question_text: The net of a prism is made from two identical octagons and a row of rectangles. How many rectangles are in the net, and how many faces, edges and vertices does the prism have?
mastery.solution_text:
An octagon has $8$ sides, so $n=8$.
Rectangles $= n$
$= 8$
Faces $= n+2$
$= 10$
Edges $= 3n$
$= 24$
Vertices $= 2n$
$= 16$

mastery.question_text: A prism has $21$ edges. Using edges $=3n$, find the number of sides of its base, name the solid, and state its number of faces and vertices.
mastery.solution_text:
Edges $= 3n$
$21 = 3n$
$n = 7$
The base has $7$ sides, so the solid is a heptagonal prism.
Faces $= n+2$
$= 9$
Vertices $= 2n$
$= 14$

mastery.question_text: A student draws two identical triangles and four rectangles and says it is the net of a triangular prism. Explain the error, and state how many rectangles a correct triangular-prism net needs.
mastery.solution_text:
A triangular prism has three rectangular side faces, one for each side of the triangle.
Rectangles needed $= n$
$= 3$
The student has drawn four rectangles, which is one too many, so the diagram would not fold up into a triangular prism.
A correct net needs exactly $3$ rectangles (with the two triangles).
